claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me begin with a few questions.

**First, how many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have one child I'd like to ask about - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know you have a son named Alex.

To assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about his circumstances.

**How old is Alex, and what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17 years old. He turned 17 back in March, so his birthday is March 15th, 2007.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school last year and hasn't gone on to college or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for clarifying that.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he does. He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that.

Before I make a final assessment, I need to check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I give you accurate information. Let me review the official Child Benefit eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the eligibility information I've reviewed, I need to ask you one more important question about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently working or earning any income, such as from a job or apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's got a full-time job at the local supermarket - works there most days of the week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one more detail to complete my assessment:

**How many hours per week does Alex work at the supermarket? Is it 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's definitely more than 24 hours - he works full-time there, so it's around 35-40 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have all the information I need to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on the information you've provided and the official Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Outcome: **Not Eligible**

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Why:** According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you stop qualifying for Child Benefit when your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training. Since Alex is working full-time (35-40 hours per week) and is not in any education or training course, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he leaves his job and enters an approved education or training course before turning 20—you may become eligible again. If you have any questions or if Alex's situation changes, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
